what: The FROZEN cumulative anchor for Band 1 on the Task 20 escalation arm. Per scene, the MEAN of that scene's Tier 3 floor arms on the four Band 1 columns -- copied out of floors.json so that a LATER arm's re-measured floors cannot move the reference the cumulative check reads. Without it the rule ratchets: four accepted 8 pp needle drifts are a collapse no single arm ever fired on.
re_measure_when: the scene, budget, resolution, step count or downscale schedule changes -- and NOT when the base depth source changes, which is the drift this anchor exists to see.
machine_change_is_NOT_a_re_measure_trigg: Pre-registration e94ee45 section 5. The pgeom entry was measured on the M5 Pro and these arms run on the M4 Max, and a change of MACHINE is not in the clause above. It also differs from these arms in three ways that are NOT the gate: dn 0.0 -> 0.05, fused -> torch loss chain, and --export-every 500. THE DATASET IS NOT ONE OF THEM -- all 593 files roll up to the same per-directory md5 on both machines. So the cumulative delta is reported DECOMPOSED: (F-mean - anchor) is everything-but-the-gate and (G0 - F-mean) is the gate. If the cumulative check fires while the per-arm check does not, what is in question is the anchor's applicability across a machine change, not the treatment.
pmask_has_no_frozen_anchor: No Tier 3 arm has ever run on work/osmo_playroom/ds. One is written from that arm's OWN F0/F1/F2 means, at the same moment floors.json is written and before G0 is scored, into <out>/anchor.json marked self_anchored. CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: for the first arm the cumulative check is VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION, because the anchor IS the floor mean and the cumulative delta equals the per-arm delta exactly. It becomes a real check for the SECOND Tier 3 arm on that scene and not before. The harness MEASURES that vacuity rather than trusting the flag, and says so in the grade.
